rows.text: [x402 reported](https://www.rzlt.io/blog/agentic-payments-2026-x402-explainer) over 165M agent transactions by April, about half of them tests.
The [median L2 fee](https://www.growthepie.com/answers/are-ethereum-l2-fees-getting-cheaper) fell from 20¢ in February 2024 to 0.06¢ in April 2026, cheap enough for machine-sized payments.

rows.signal: Volume with tests and wash trades removed
rows.text: On [Allium's strictest filter](https://nevermined.ai/blog/stablecoin-payments-ai-agents-statistics), real agent volume is near $1.6M a month.

The [OCC stablecoin rule](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-92.html) takes effect 2027-01-18. A [procedural vote](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/crypto-market-structure-bill-fails-in-senate-vote-49-50) on the market-structure bill failed 49 to 50 on 2026-09-15.

rows.signal: Who pays when an agent exceeds its mandate
rows.text: [Unsettled](https://worldpay.com/en/insights/articles/agentic-commerce-liability-is-still-being-written): without a record of what the user asked, a dispute is close to a coin flip. My view: the first network rule that requires an intent record decides it.

Volume is the lagging bet. The liability rule is the leading one. My read: 1 in 3 that Visa, Mastercard or a top-10 US card issuer has a rule in effect by 2027-06-30 requiring a record of what the user told the agent. Announcements without an effective date do not count. Gravity can resolve it; I will post the outcome either way.

If the rule is late, the loss is small: about 2.7 weeks of my time. ARCS already writes an append-only record for human decisions, not yet a signed agent mandate. Long the liability record layer; short raw counts as proof of use.
Holds. The stake is a public call, not a build; any build is time-boxed.
Leaked: no resolution rule, so the odds read 0.24 to 0.62 by wording. Fixed: the rule above. As written, the middle 90% of runs is 0.17 to 0.46; 1 in 3 sits inside.
Leaks: the base rate of a network rule drives most of the spread. I re-mark the odds at each Visa and Mastercard rules release.
Leaked: I build the remedy and grade my own call. Fixed: the interest is stated, Gravity resolves, and the Put no longer overstates what ARCS writes.

groups.label: How I could read it wrong

rows.text: Tests and self-dealing loops inflate the count, so I discount it by the half that is tests.

Visa and Mastercard run agent payments on tokenized cards ([PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/credit-cards/2026/cards-make-their-case-in-an-agentic-world/)). None of it shows on-chain, so on-chain volume undercounts agent demand.
An operator's agents paying its own services look like wash trades, so the strict filter may drop real use. I have not tested this.
The strict filter removes tests and wash trades, not illicit flow: it cannot tell compliant volume from illicit volume.

sections.tagline: What I would do in the first week.

blocks.text: [Your Idea Engine post](https://kylelibra.substack.com/p/how-to-find-startup-ideas): a good memo now comes 6x faster, and some still come out unusable. Ideas are getting cheap. Trusting them is not. ARCS builds conviction the way an oak builds rings: every pass with its reason, every kill test written before it runs, every overturned belief kept on the record. The rings are what hold the tree up.

cards.title: The agent-payments wedge
cards.text: When an AI agent sends stablecoins, the send is final. Policy engines log which rule allowed it, not what the agent intended or whether it came true. ARCS already writes a cousin of that record for human decisions: what was asked, why, and what happened.

tabs.lede: Your open application asks what I would own that you don't staff today, and why you'd move faster with me. My answer: a hatch desk, sketched to build with you, in the open.

blocks.text: Most funds call it a deal desk. I would run it as an AI-native platform team that compounds: each memo, its kill criteria, the record of every call.
Every pass is logged with its reasons and rechecked as markets move. A wrong pass surfaces before you miss the next one like it. The call stays yours, and comes faster.
It sits on top of your Idea Engine: the agents find and draft, the desk keeps the record. Nothing gets built twice.
